findings.claim: The positive list is not closed: its comment-line exemption tests only a line's first non-blank characters, the declaration regex matches a line wherever it sits (inside a block comment or a template literal), and the freeze line is only counted, never placed. So seven measured shapes pass parseAllowListSource with zero violations and report the ruling's pair, yet the runtime list holds a third hash; the freeze does not catch them, because each widens before the freeze statement runs or the freeze never runs. Two of them were run end-to-end: the mutated harness admits iv on a hash the ruling did not name, where the committed harness exits 2 (A3a). The README (line 8) says 'the runtime list is the literal or the run dies', and the fold says every write throws 'whatever the route'. Both hold only for writes after Object.freeze executes. A0 cannot see this: none of its twenty-one wrong sources exercises the comment exemption, freeze placement or a decoy declaration, so the positive list does not make the probe-set question moot. The two exemptions and the count-only freeze rule are negative carve-outs inside the positive list. This is a control-strength gap, not a harness defect: the committed harness's declaration (line 214) and freeze (line 219) are correct.
findings.counterexample: Leg probe (leg-3044-scratch-3/probe.mjs, parseAllowListSource taken verbatim from the 41f25098 blob, each source imported as an ESM module). All seven report grammarViolations [] and grammarHashes [2266fc0dfe824f24, 87aff037d7de47a7], and admit 0123456789abcdef at runtime. (1) The line '/* c */ R4_SEVERITY_LOWERING_RULES.push(x);' between the declaration and the freeze line. (2) 'const y = 1' then a line '* R4_SEVERITY_LOWERING_RULES.push(x);' before the freeze (a multiplication continuation). (3) A multi-line template literal whose interior line is '* ${R4_SEVERITY_LOWERING_RULES.push(x)}', before the freeze. (4) The pair declaration inside a block comment as the decoy, then '/* */ export const R4_SEVERITY_LOWERING_RULES = [pair plus x];' and the freeze line (runtime list frozen with three hashes). (5) The same decoy inside a template literal. (6) 'if (0)' on the line before the freeze line, then a '/* */'-prefixed push (frozen false). (7) The freeze line inside a block comment, then a '/* */'-prefixed push (frozen false). End to end, two harness copies built in scratch: h-commentPrefix inserts '/* r4 */ R4_SEVERITY_LOWERING_RULES.push(54140f59be3e6e44 quoted);' before mig-harness.mjs:219, and h-decoy is shape (4) with 54140f59be3e6e44. Each was run with A3a's own invocation (--set manifest-2263305c.json --only 54140f59 --inventory run/inv/a3a.json --rules run/rules-a3). Each passes the grammar with 0 violations, exits 0, writes 1 row and prints 'fidelity: severity (inventory iv: lowered under R4) (expected)'; the committed harness exits 2 on the same input. Measured as refused or harmless: includes then push on one line (the second occurrence is refused); a trailing-space second declaration (refused, and a SyntaxError); a renamed re-export (refused); CRLF (accepted, correct); a Cyrillic look-alike identifier (accepted; it does not touch the real list); an Array.prototype.includes override (accepted, admits every hash: the stated limit). After the freeze, push, defineProperty and setPrototypeOf each throw TypeError. Fix shape (not built): drop the '/*' and '*' exemptions and admit only '//' lines. The committed harness names the identifier on no '/*' or '*' line (lines 31, 214, 219, 279, 292, 294), so this costs nothing. Require the freeze line to follow the declaration line with only '//' lines between, which also refuses a decoy declaration, because the real one then needs an exempt or refused line. Add the seven shapes to A0's wrong set and correct the README sentence.

findings.claim: A0's own narration miscounts its probe set. The comment at lines 456-460 says 'twenty wrong sources: the five read 1 named and the eleven widening shapes read 2 named, plus a missing freeze, a double declaration, an indexed write and a shadowing binding'. The object holds twenty-one (the expect at the arm's end asserts 21), and the comment omits the repeat probe. 'The eleven widening shapes read 2 named' (the comment, the README line 8 and the fold's message) is inexact: the set's lengthWrite probe is one read 2 called non-widening, and read 2's '.some((h, i, a) => a.splice(0, 0, x))' shape is not probed.
findings.counterexample: Read 2's deposit (leg-3044-read2.json, 3044-r2-F1) lists the eleven as: space before the dot, newline before the dot, optional chaining, an inline comment split, an includes assignment, an alias, Array.prototype.push.call, Object.assign, Reflect.set, a forEach callback push and a some callback splice. It adds that '.length = 3 also passes and mutates the array (no widening)'. A0's wrong set has lengthWrite and no some-callback probe. The positive list refuses the some shape (a '.some(' member is not an allowed form), so this is narration accuracy, not a gap.

verdict: read 3 on 41f25098 (scoped to A0 and the declaration): as typed, 0 BLOCKING, 1 MATERIAL, 1 MINOR, 0 QUESTION; F1 and F2 folded in af0b0ba5: only a line whose first non-blank characters are // is exempt (block-comment lines are not, since a line's first characters cannot tell a comment from code that follows one); the freeze line is PLACED, the first non-// line after the declaration, so nothing can run between the literal and the freeze and a freeze elsewhere falls under the code-line rule; a column-0 declaration anywhere counts, so a decoy inside a block comment or a template literal is a second declaration and is refused; the seven shapes this read named, the some-splice shape read 2 named and a block-comment mention join the probe set (thirty wrong sources, each built on a valid base that itself passes); the narration and the README counts are corrected. The harness source is unchanged by this fold (its declaration at line 214, four // lines, the freeze at line 219, and the identifier on no block-comment line). Convergence, named by the orchestrator: three reads have held the harness's behaviour (byte-identical old-versus-new output over K3, batches 1 to 4 and the full set; every arm discriminating; the freeze breaking nothing); reads 1 to 3 each tightened the strength of a source grammar whose purpose is a parity sensor over a two-hash list in a reviewed commit. This fold adds no claim beyond what read 3 measured: the seven shapes it named are now refused by the committed controls run, which is the measurement a read 4 would repeat. The remaining limit is the one stated in the README and the header, a mutation that never names the identifier, which no source grammar can see and which the runtime freeze answers for every write after it. The chain is named converged here; no read 4 is dispatched. Mergeable.
